title: Rules as classifiers: checkable "when" predicates measured on the v3 training halves (round 2)
verdict_cn:
结论：这个方向可行性低，只建议保留其中几项便宜的检查。它的设想是给每条规则写一个能检查的"适用条件"，用来挑选检验题、剔除"死题"（所有版本都做不对的题）。
做了什么：给第三版实验流程（v3）的49条候选规则逐条写了适用条件，其中38条能在解题前检查。用GLM（一种大语言模型）当"适用性裁判"，在训练题上判了4,595次，约花251万token（模型的计费单位），没有调用解题模型。
发现：
1. 裁判本身可靠：同一题连判三次完全一致的占87%，与人工判断一致的约占89%。
2. 条件挑不准：条件选中的题里，规则所针对的错误类型的比例和随机挑差不多。
3. 剔不掉死题：被排除的死题30/71，被误排除的其他题21/72，差别不显著；筛完仍有45%是死题。
4. 规则在"适用"题上引起的变化（19.4%）并不比在"不适用"题上（18.9%）多，和随机波动分不开。
5. 若按第四版流程（v4）的计划把所有"适用"题都放进检验，题量变成4.5倍，解题花费约2.7倍，有用信息反而更稀。
建议：把条件作为规则的固定字段；检查规则引用的证据题是否满足它自己的条件（38条里有20条不满足），这一步不花解题费用；把"适用题与不适用题的变化差"作为诊断报告。死题问题要靠统计方法和抽样来解决，不要靠条件筛选。
what_i_did:
**Inputs and setup**
- Read the shared context and obeyed its hard rules. Only training paths of the completed v3 run were opened. Nothing was written under run directories or the repository.
- Re-derived from the cells the facts that D4 depends on:
  - 49 proposals and 15 screened rules (15 screen arms + 2 confirm arms); 2 screen passes and 0 confirmed.
  - 143 trigger items. For all 38 rules that reached a trigger computation, the trigger set equals my recomputation from the codes.
  - 71 dead items under the strict definition. The context's 72 includes spreadsheetbench/37456, which has one unknown cell.

**Conditions and judge runs**
- Wrote one "when" condition per proposal from the rule text only: 28 judged (5 narrowings of literally-always rules), 10 mechanical exact features, 7 always, 3 runtime, 1 without a target code.
- Ran a GLM-5.3 reason-then-label applicability judge over each stage's whole check half: 3 identical votes for the 13 screened judged conditions (908 items), 1 vote for the other 15. 3,431 calls, plus a 28-call smoke test.
- Ran a writer swap: the first attempt's GLM-drafted conditions under the same judge, 800 calls.
- Ran an evidence-coverage pass: each condition on its own rule's evidence items, 3 votes, 336 calls.
- Computed the mechanical features from the training items and the SpreadsheetBench input workbooks.

**Agreement checks**
- Labelled 2 x 30 items blind, before seeing the votes.
- Cross-checked against the first attempt's 120 manual labels and its judge.

**Analysis**
- Precision, recall, lift and an exact Fisher test against the target codes for 48 rules.
- Dead items: exclusion counts and a cross-tab of training pattern against outcome.
- The first attempt's "parent + one control" probe, re-tested.
- In-scope vs out-of-scope rule-vs-parent movement for the 13 non-trivial screened rules: a stratified permutation test (20,000 permutations), parent-instability and other-arm controls, and per-rule tests.
- Replication between the check half and the proposal half, and between the screen and confirm rounds.
- Five panel designs: items, movers, cells, solver tokens from measured per-cell means, and a sign-flip null probability that a no-effect rule passes the C1 "gain >= 1 item" part.
- Judge stability, Fleiss kappa, agreement with independent readers, and writer agreement (Cohen kappa).
- Verified the AutoGuide reference by web search.

**Output**
- Wrote the full English report and preserved the first attempt's report unchanged.
- The first attempt recommended the "parent + one control" probe; this round refutes it.
evidence:
All [M] unless marked; check halves: SearchQA 99-100, OfficeQA 36-37, LiveMath 49, SpreadsheetBench 45, ALFWorld 28 items.

(1) Checkable conditions
- 38/49 proposals are checkable before any solver call.
- 12/49 (24%) literally state no condition.
- 6 conditions hold on at least 27/28 or 42/49 of their check half, i.e. "always" in disguise. Example: E-ds s3-r2/s3-r3 hold on 48/49.

(2) Precision against the target codes (40 scorable non-trivial rows)
- Lift >= 1.5 in 11 rows, lift < 1 in 14. Median lift of the 27 judged rows: 1.02. Median share of the check half matched: 57%.
- Fisher p < 0.05 in 4/40 rows (about 2 expected by chance), all of them mechanical:
  - LiveMath "meta-option present": precision 0.96/0.95, recall 1.00, base 0.45/0.43. This holds by definition, since code D1 is "did not pick the meta-option".
  - I-ds s2-r2 "two or more editions": precision 0.37, base 0.22.
  - E-ds s5-r4 "clean/heat/cool task": precision 0.33, base 0.18.
- Screened judged conditions sit at the base rate. Examples: person 0.12 vs 0.11; key match 0.32 vs 0.33.

(3) Dead items (15 screened rules, 143 trigger items)
- Outcomes: 71 dead, 22 up, 19 down, 31 ties.
- Training pattern: failed both runs, 58/94 dead; passed one run, 2/19 dead. But 14 of the 22 up items also failed both training runs.
- Conditions exclude 30/71 dead vs 21/72 others (p = 0.12) and keep 16/22 up items. The filtered panel is still 41/92 (45%) dead.
- 51 of the 123 non-trivial trigger items (41%) lie outside their own rule's condition.
- The probe "parent and control 1 fail every trigger run" drops 92/143 items: all 71 dead, but also 11 of the 22 up items. This refutes the first attempt's recommendation.

(4) Do rules act where their condition holds? (13 non-trivial screened rules, whole check half, runs 0..GATE_RUNS-1)
- Own-arm movement: 98/505 (19.4%) in scope vs 76/402 (18.9%) out of scope. Permutation p = 0.60; net -2.5 vs +2.5 (p = 0.72).
- Parent unstable: 109/505 vs 89/403.
- Other screened arms on the same scope: 141/788 vs 190/875.
- Only I-ds s1-r1 (surname-only answers) concentrates: 8/26 vs 6/74 (p = 0.008), with 2 up and 6 down in scope, i.e. harm. It is not significant after Bonferroni over 13 rules.
- Replication fails:
  - E-ds s1-r1 (a screen passer): check half +4.5 (17/12), proposal half -7.0 (6/17, p = 0.035), confirm -1.0 / -4.5.
  - E-ds s1-r2: +7.5 vs +2.5.
  - I-ds s3-r2: 0.0 vs -5.5 (0/9, p = 0.004).
  - Overall, 2 of 34 sign tests have p < 0.05, against 1.7 expected.

(5) Panel designs (15 screened rules)

| design | items | movers | C1 cells | movers per 1,000 cells | solver tokens [E] | null P(pass gain part) | observed passes / null expectation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v3 trigger | 142 | 33 | 2,892 | 11.4 | 33.3M | 0.26 | 4 / 3.8 |
| v4 all in-scope | 632 | 129 | 14,172 | 9.1 | 89.2M | 0.36 | 5 / 5.4 |
| scope-filtered trigger | 92 | 24 | 1,824 | 13.2 | 29.8M | 0.23 | - |
| whole check half | 1,034 | 205 | - | 8.8 | - | 0.39 | - |

- Solver tokens per gate cell (measured): SearchQA 2,603; OfficeQA 5,626; LiveMath 3,043; SpreadsheetBench 3,820; ALFWorld 141,157.

(6) Judge reliability
- 3 identical votes on 908 items: unanimous 792 (87.2%); the first vote equals the majority on 874 (96.3%). Fleiss kappa 0.17-0.92; the low values are the prevalence paradox at 48/49 positive.
- The majority agrees with an independent reader on 160/180 items (88.9%), and on 143/156 (91.7%) items the reader marked certain.
- Parse rate: 4,595/4,595.
- Cost per call: SearchQA 408 tokens, OfficeQA 456, LiveMath 1,151, SpreadsheetBench 502, ALFWorld 383.

(7) Writer sensitivity
- Regex predicates vs mine, 29 pairs: median Cohen kappa 0.27.
- GLM-written vs mine, 11 rules: 628/772 items agree (81%), median kappa 0.66. One outright misreading: E-ds s3-r2, kappa 0.03, precision 0.

(8) Evidence coverage
- 126/159 evidence items covered, against 87.3 expected by chance.
- 20/38 rules leave at least one of their own evidence items outside their condition; 3 cover less than half.
design:
Narrowed D4 for v5: conditions as instrumentation, not as a panel generator.

1. Typed condition field, frozen with the rule text.
   - Types: mechanical (an exact feature computed by code, preferred), judged (natural language over solver-visible task fields), always, runtime.
   - A judged condition that holds on >= 90% of the check half is treated as always.
2. Applicability judge.
   - GLM, reason-then-label JSON, 2 votes plus a third on disagreement. That is about 2.1 calls per item and reproduces the 3-vote majority exactly.
   - If unanimity on the check half is below 85%, ask the analyst once to sharpen the condition, showing the split items.
3. Evidence-coverage gate, with zero solver cost. Every cited evidence item must satisfy the rule's own condition; otherwise re-ask with the uncovered items, using v4's validator-feedback re-ask.
4. Trigger panel = v3 code-based check-half failures AND the condition (the scope-filtered trigger).
   - Measured: 92 vs 142 items, 13.2 vs 11.4 movers per 1,000 cells, -37% C1 cells, -10% tokens.
   - Out-of-scope code-matched failures are reported separately, as a generalization check.
5. Scope-specificity diagnostic for every screened rule, with zero extra solver calls because rule and parent already cover the focal panel.
   - Compare in-scope vs out-of-scope rule-vs-parent discordance, with parent-instability and other-arm controls.
   - Flag "no mechanism evidence" when the in-scope rate is not above both. Report only, until D8 calibrates it.
6. C2 harm reported separately in scope; I-ds s1-r1's harm sits there.
7. Do NOT replace trigger panels by "all in-scope check-half items" under the fixed "gain >= 1 whole item" C1 threshold.
   - It costs 4.9x the cells and about 2.7x the tokens, with a lower yield.
   - Its null pass rate is 0.36 vs 0.26.
   - If v4 keeps it, it needs a calibrated paired test (D8).
8. No pre-classifier for dead items.
   - They add zero paired difference, so they cost calls, not power.
   - Cost levers belong to D1 (fresh batches), D5 (noise) and D8 (run allocation by power).
9. Exact structural features go to D7, e.g. LiveMath "meta-option present": precision 0.95-0.96, recall 1.00 for code D1. It is the natural condition for structural, non-leaking rules.

Re-running the r2 scripts on v4 data, where the conditions come from the analyst's own when-clauses, tests the one open question at zero solver cost: whether template rules act more in scope.

pilot.result:
**What ran**
- 4,595 GLM-5.3 judge calls on training check halves, 2,514,148 tokens, 100% parsed:
  - main pass 3,431 calls (3 votes for 13 screened conditions, 1 vote for 15 others);
  - smoke test 28;
  - GLM-written-condition swap 800;
  - evidence coverage 336.
- No solver calls.
- The first attempt in this direction used another 276,852 tokens (529 calls, re-verified), so D4 used about 2.79M tokens in total.

**Outcome**
- The judge is reliable: 87.2% unanimous, and 88.9% agreement with independent readers.
- The conditions do not discriminate target-code failures: median lift 1.02.
- They do not remove dead items: 30/71 dead vs 21/72 others excluded (p = 0.12).
- Rules do not act more in scope: 19.4% vs 18.9% movement (p = 0.60).
- The v4 all-in-scope panel costs 4.9x the cells for a lower yield.

risks:
**Validity of the inputs**
- The conditions are post hoc. I wrote them from the rule texts without looking at outcomes, but knowing the project's results.
- Another writer gives materially different panels: GLM vs me kappa median 0.66; regex vs me 0.27. Panel membership therefore depends on who writes the condition.
- The examiner codes are per-run GLM diagnoses whose reliability is unmeasured. Precision against noisy codes underestimates true precision. The in-scope vs out-of-scope movement result does not depend on the codes.
- v3 rules were not written in the v4 conditional template ("when X: do Y; otherwise default"). Template rules might confine their effects to scope. This is untested and needs v4 data.

**Small samples**
- 15 screened rules, 13 of them non-trivial; 143 trigger items; check halves of 28-49 items outside SearchQA.
- Per-rule tests are weak. The pooled in-vs-out 95% interval is roughly -4.6 to +5.6 percentage points (unstratified estimate), so only an in-scope concentration above about 6 points is excluded.

**Measurement limits**
- Movement was measured at 2 runs (SearchQA, OfficeQA, LiveMath) or 1 run (SpreadsheetBench, ALFWorld), which undercounts movers by a factor of about 1.24.
- The null pass model covers only the gain part of C1, not the control margin.
- Deadness of non-trigger items is unknown, because the controls never ran on them.
- The judge sees task fields only, not SearchQA snippets, OfficeQA pages or ALFWorld trajectories.
- The judge, examiner and analyst are all GLM-5.3, so their errors may be correlated.

**Cost figures**
- Solver-token figures are cells times measured mean tokens per cell, not exact. They are dominated by ALFWorld at 141k tokens per cell.

**Design risk**
- Adopting the v4 all-in-scope panel with the fixed one-item threshold would raise cost about 2.7x and raise the false-pass probability of the gain part (0.26 to 0.36), without adding signal.
cost_estimate:
**Spent (measured)**

| item | GLM calls | tokens |
|---|---|---|
| this round | 4,595 | 2,514,148 |
| first attempt | 529 | 276,852 |
| D4 total | 5,124 | 2,791,000 |

- No solver calls.

**Narrowed D4 in v5 (estimated)**
- 5 rules x the check half x 3 votes per chain, over the five stages:

| benchmark | tokens per chain |
|---|---|
| SearchQA | 0.61M |
| OfficeQA | 0.25M |
| LiveMath | 0.85M |
| SpreadsheetBench | 0.34M |
| ALFWorld | 0.16M |
| total | about 2.2M |

- Both chains: about 4.4M, roughly 3% of the v3 run's 139M.
- With 2+1 voting: about 1.55M per chain.
- Evidence-coverage gate: about 0.1M per chain.
- Mechanical conditions, the scope-specificity diagnostic and in-scope harm reporting cost zero solver tokens.
- The scope-filtered trigger panel saves about 10% of the C1 solver tokens (29.8M vs 33.3M for the 15 v3 screened rules).

**The design to avoid (estimated)**
- The v4 all-in-scope C1 panel would cost about 89M vs 33M solver tokens for the same 15 rules (+56M), for a lower yield per cell.
recommendation:
**Do not adopt D4 as a mechanism for selecting panels or removing dead items.** The v3 training data refutes all three premises:
- the conditions do not classify the targeted failures (median lift 1.02);
- they do not separate dead items (p = 0.12);
- rules do not act more where their condition holds (19.4% vs 18.9%, p = 0.60).

**Keep the cheap instrumentation in v5.**
- Typed conditions frozen with the rule.
- A GLM reason-then-label judge with 2+1 votes, using unanimity below 85% as a vagueness flag.
- The evidence-coverage gate (20/38 v3 conditions would have been sent back).
- The scope-filtered trigger: modest savings, 13.2 vs 11.4 movers per 1,000 cells.
- In-scope harm reporting.
- A per-rule scope-specificity diagnostic.

**Tell the v4 workflow** that the planned "trigger items = all in-scope check-half items" panel is 4.5x the items, 4.9x the cells and about 2.7x the solver tokens of v3's trigger panel, with a lower yield. It should not run under the fixed "gain >= 1 whole item" C1 threshold. Hand the threshold to D8 for a calibrated paired test.

**Route the remaining questions elsewhere.**
- Dead items: D1/D5/D8. In a paired test they cost calls, not power.
- The exact LiveMath "meta-option present" condition: D7.

**Once v4 data exists,** re-run the r2 scripts unchanged at zero solver cost, to test the one open question: whether template-conditioned rules act more in scope than v3 rules.
